name: Marketing Manager and Sales Professional
description: ⚠⚠⚠ $166,790, among the highest medians of any bachelor's-entry occupation on this site — beside computer and information systems management at $175,140 and computer hardware engineering at $161,740 — and 80% of employers report a bachelor's rather than a master's. ⚠⚠ The way in is the other half of this page: market research and marketing specialist roles number 941,700 with 87,200 openings a year, and sales representatives 1,571,400 with 123,400.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠ NOTHING HERE IS LICENSED, NO MAJOR IS REQUIRED, AND THE MASTER'S IS NOT WHAT PROMOTES YOU. O*NET's employer data for marketing managers: 80% bachelor's, 12% high school diploma, 6% master's. ⚠ Compare market research analysts and marketing specialists — a more junior, more analytical role — at 70% bachelor's and 30% MASTER'S. ⚠⚠⚠ The graduate degree is associated with the specialist track, not the management one. If you want it, want it for the analytics. ⚠⚠ THE ENTRANT DATA SAYS THE SAME THING ABOUT THE MAJOR. Census ACS microdata (2024) on the undergraduate fields held by marketing managers: BUSINESS 175,070, COMMUNICATIONS 88,800, SOCIAL SCIENCES 38,529. ⚠ Communications at half of business is a substantial and underadvertised second feeder. Attainment: bachelor's 354,402, graduate degree 144,540, and ⚠⚠ SOME COLLEGE AND NO DEGREE 51,488 — roughly one marketing manager in nine reached the job without finishing a degree, which is unusual at this median. ⚠ Note the two sources disagree in a legible way: employers say 6% need a master's, while 144,540 managers hold a graduate degree. Employers report what is REQUIRED; the census records what people HOLD. Both are true.

⚠⚠⚠ The ladder, and the top of it is reached on a bachelor's

Market research analyst / marketing specialist13-1161$78,760941,700✅ 87,200✅ much faster (7%+)70% bachelor's, 30% master's
✅✅ Marketing manager11-2021✅✅ $166,790407,00034,300✅ much faster (7%+)⚠ 80% bachelor's, 6% master's

⚠⚠⚠ $166,790 is among the highest medians of any bachelor's-entry occupation on this site — beside computer and information systems management at $175,140 and computer hardware engineering at $161,740 — and it is reached with a bachelor's and experience rather than a further degree.

⚠⚠ Look at the master's column twice. Marketing managers: 6% master's. Market research analysts, one rung DOWN: 30%. The graduate degree attaches to the analytical specialism, not to the promotion. That is the opposite of most paths on this site and it should change how you spend money.

⚠⚠⚠ $32,840 for selling something technical

Wholesale and manufacturing sales representatives are 1,571,400 jobs with about 123,400 openings a year — among the largest openings figures on this site — in an occupation projected to show little or no change from 2025 to 2035. That is turnover, and it means the door is always open.

Which products you sellMedianTypical entry
⚠ Except technical and scientific$72,080high school diploma
✅ Technical and scientific✅ $104,920✅ bachelor's degree

⚠⚠⚠ Same occupation, $32,840 apart, and the split is whether the product needs explaining. Medical devices, laboratory instruments, industrial equipment, software, pharmaceuticals.

⚠⚠ The practical consequence is worth stating plainly: a science, engineering or health background is worth real money in sales. If you have one and the laboratory or the ward is not for you, this is the best-paid use of it outside the field itself — and this site's health and engineering paths are full of people who should know that.

⚠⚠ What marketing managers actually studied

Undergraduate fieldPeople
Business175,070
⚠ Communications88,800
Social sciences38,529

⚠ Communications at roughly half of business is a bigger feeder than most advice admits, and social sciences third is the same pattern this site found on law and on health administration — the general analytical degrees travel further than their titles suggest.

Attainment: bachelor's 354,402, graduate degree 144,540, and ⚠⚠ some college with no degree 51,488.

⚠⚠⚠ Roughly one marketing manager in nine got there without finishing a degree. At a $166,790 median that is genuinely unusual, and it is consistent with O*NET recording 12% of employers accepting a high school diploma. This is a field where demonstrated results outrank credentials more than almost anywhere else on this site.

⚠⚠⚠ Florida numbers Principles of Marketing twice, and it can cost you a course

NumberCarriersSector
MAR2011 Principles of Marketing24⚠⚠ ALL 24 are state colleges
MAR3023 Principles of Marketing1911 universities + 8 state colleges

⚠⚠⚠ Same course title, two numbers, split on the sector line — and a 2000-level course cannot supply upper-division hours toward a Florida baccalaureate. A student who takes MAR2011 at a state college and transfers into a marketing BBA may be asked to take the same subject again at the 3000 level.

⚠ The eight state colleges that carry BOTH numbers are the evidence that this is a deliberate A.S.-to-baccalaureate ladder rather than a filing error — they run both credentials. It costs a transferring student either way.

⚠⚠ So get a written answer from the receiving department before you enrol, and if the baccalaureate is the goal, ask whether you should wait and take MAR3023.

Necessary skills

  • Reading a market as evidence rather than as opinion — which is why the research course matters more than the creative one.
  • Pricing and margin. O*NET puts developing pricing strategies among the first tasks of the job, and it is where marketing meets the accounts.
  • Measurement and attribution. The specialist half of this field has become quantitative, and the people who can prove an effect get the budget.
  • Selling — genuinely. Whatever your title, you will spend your career persuading people with their own priorities.
  • Writing that survives being cut in half, because most marketing output is short.
  • Tolerance for being measured. This is a field with numbers attached to your name, which suits some people and not others.

Advice

⚠⚠⚠ Do not buy a master's to become a manager. 80% of employers want a bachelor's and 6% a master's. If you want the graduate degree, want it for the analytical track, where 30% of employers do ask.

⚠⚠ If you have a technical or scientific background, look at technical sales before anything else. $104,920 against $72,080 for the same occupation, and 123,400 openings a year. It is the single best-paid use of a science degree outside the science.

⚠ Take the research course. MAR4613 Marketing Research and Information Systems is carried by 13 Florida institutions and it is what separates a marketing graduate from 2,301 others in the same year.

⚠⚠ Watch the two Principles of Marketing numbers. MAR2011 at a state college is lower division; MAR3023 is upper division. If a baccalaureate is the plan, confirm which one counts before you register.

And take the entry roles seriously rather than as a waiting room. 87,200 marketing specialist openings and 123,400 sales openings a year is where essentially everyone starts, and the management median at the top of this page is earned there.

programs.note: The named degree — 21 Florida public institutions, 2,688 credentials, 2,302 of them bachelor's and only 162 master's, which matches what employers ask for. ⚠⚠ Read its degrees note on the MAR2011 / MAR3023 sector split before taking Principles of Marketing at a state college.

⚠⚠ The largest real feeder: Census microdata puts BUSINESS first among the undergraduate fields held by marketing managers at 175,070 people, ahead of communications at 88,800. ⚠ A general business degree with marketing coursework competes for the same jobs and is taught more widely across Florida.

⚠⚠ Where the specialist half of this field has gone. Market research analysts and marketing specialists number 941,700 with 87,200 annual openings, and the work is measurement, segmentation and attribution. ⚠ It is also where the 30% master's demand sits — if you are buying a graduate degree, buy it here rather than for management.
⚠ Named because pricing and margin responsibility are what separate a $166,790 manager from a $78,760 specialist, and O*NET lists developing pricing strategies among the first tasks of the job.

⚠⚠ Named for one specific and well-paid reason: technical and scientific sales representatives earn $104,920 against $72,080 for the non-technical half of the same occupation. A technical degree plus the ability to sell is one of the better-paid combinations available on a bachelor's.

courses.reason: ⚠⚠ Principles of Marketing — 24 Florida institutions, and every single one is a STATE COLLEGE. The lower-division version, and the cheapest way into the subject.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠⚠ This is a 2000-level course and cannot supply upper-division hours toward a Florida baccalaureate. If you intend to transfer into a marketing BBA, get a written answer from the receiving department first — you may be asked to take MAR3023, the same subject, again.

courses.reason: ⚠⚠ Principles of Marketing — 19 institutions: 11 universities and the 8 state colleges that hold baccalaureate authority. The upper-division version, and the one that counts toward a bachelor's.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Eight state colleges carry BOTH this and MAR2011, which is the evidence that the pair is a deliberate A.S.-to-baccalaureate ladder rather than a numbering error.

courses.reason: ⚠⚠ Marketing Research and Information Systems — 13 institutions, the most widely carried upper-division marketing course after the principles pair. ⚠ The research and measurement skill is what distinguishes a graduate in a field producing 2,302 bachelor's a year.
Consumer Behavior — 8 institutions. The psychology underneath the discipline, and the course that makes segmentation more than guesswork.
⚠ Sales Management — 8 institutions. Named deliberately: sales is where 1,571,400 jobs and 123,400 annual openings are, and most marketing graduates start there whether or not they planned to.
International Marketing — 9 institutions. Relevant in Florida specifically, given Miami's role as a Latin American commercial hub.
Services Marketing — 8 institutions. Florida's economy is overwhelmingly services — tourism, health care, financial services — and this is the course that addresses it.
Marketing for Managers — 8 institutions, all state colleges. The applied version for students in a business A.S. or BAS rather than a marketing major.
Personal Selling — 8 institutions. ⚠ The most practical course on this page: selling is what the largest occupation in the family actually does, and it is teachable.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also numbered MKA1021 Principles of Selling at 4 institutions. Register by number.

courses.reason: Principles of Advertising — 8 institutions. The promotional side, and the lower-division entry to it at state colleges.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also numbered MKA1511 Advertising: Traditional and New Media at 3 institutions.

courses.reason: ⚠ Elementary Statistics — 39 institutions. Market research and attribution are statistical work, and the 30% of employers who want a master's in the analytical track want it for this.
Financial Accounting — 32 institutions. Pricing and margin decisions are the manager's job, and you cannot make them without reading the statements.
Principles of Microeconomics — 39 institutions. Demand, elasticity and competition — the theory underneath every pricing decision the job description names.
English Composition I — 39 institutions. Most marketing output is short written work, and clarity under a word limit is the professional skill.

Fundamentals of Speech Communication — 16 institutions. Named because communications is the second-largest feeder into this occupation at 88,800 people, and because presenting is most of the job at every level.
Computer Applications for Business — the spreadsheet and data-handling foundation. ⚠ Named because marketing has become a measurement discipline and the specialist roles screen on it.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida numbers business computing several ways (CGS2100, CGS1100, ISM3011). Check your catalogue.
